goal.problem: The new folder-per-type scribe layout has no mechanism to recover from index corruption or create periodic backups of index state.
goal.solution: Add a notes.py repair subcommand that rebuilds indexes from .md files, and a backup script that snapshots all indexes daily.
goal.value: Provides resilience against data loss — indexes can be rebuilt from the source .md files, and daily backups provide point-in-time recovery.

components.name: repair subcommand
components.description: notes.py repair — scans all type folders for .md files, cross-references with index.jsonl entries, rebuilds missing entries, removes orphan entries, and regenerates next_id from max observed ID.

components.name: backup script
components.description: scribe/backup_indexes.py — copies all index.jsonl files to backups/<date>/ subfolder. Retains last N backups (configurable, default 30). Can be invoked by cron.

components.name: Backup pruning
components.description: Old backups beyond retention window are deleted automatically when a new backup is created.

shape.integration_point: notes.py repair — new subcommand in existing CLI. scribe/backup_indexes.py — standalone script.
shape.pattern: repair follows the same argparse subcommand pattern as other notes.py commands. Backup script is standalone like other scripts/.
shape.data_flow: repair: glob *.md files in each type folder -> compare with index.jsonl entries -> rebuild index. backup: read all index.jsonl -> write copies to backups/<date>/.
shape.dependencies: Phases 1-4 complete (folder-per-type layout is active and populated).

behavior.processing: Repair: 1. For each type folder, glob *.md files. 2. Read index.jsonl entries. 3. For .md files without index entries: create minimal index entry (id from filename, status='active', timestamp from file mtime, summary from first 200 chars of content). 4. For index entries without .md files: flag as orphan, optionally remove. 5. Rebuild next_id from max ID. 6. Write corrected indexes. Backup: 1. Create backups/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ dir. 2. Copy each type's index.jsonl. 3. Delete backup dirs older than retention window.
behavior.output: repair: report of fixes applied (N entries rebuilt, M orphans found, next_id reset to K). backup: confirmation of backup created, N old backups pruned.

error_cases.behavior: repair prints 'No scribe data found', exits 0.

error_cases.trigger: .md filename is not a valid integer
error_cases.behavior: Skip with warning (could be a non-note file).

error_cases.trigger: Backup dir already exists for today

edge_cases.behavior: Report what would be fixed, make no changes.
Repair scans archive/ subfolders with the same logic.
Keep no old backups, only the current one.

in_scope: Unit tests for repair logic and backup
out_of_scope: Cron job setup for backup scheduling — documented but not automated
Repair of memory/ layout — separate system
Recovery from backup (manual process, just copy files back)
must_not_break: Existing index data — repair only adds missing entries or removes orphans
Running notes.py commands during repair — FileLock prevents conflicts

acceptance_criteria: Given an index.jsonl missing entries for some .md files, when repair runs, then the missing entries are recreated with correct IDs and summaries
Given an index.jsonl with entries pointing to deleted .md files, when repair runs, then orphan entries are flagged and reported
Given next_id is incorrect (lower than max existing ID), when repair runs, then next_id is reset to max_id + 1
Given --dry-run flag, when repair runs, then it reports issues but makes no changes to any files
Given repair runs on archive/ subfolders, then the same rebuild logic applies to archived notes
Given backup_indexes.py runs, then backups/<today>/ contains a copy of every type's index.jsonl
Given 35 backup dirs exist and --retain 30, when backup runs, then the 5 oldest are deleted
Given backup dir for today already exists, when backup runs again, then it overwrites without error
